Rashi on Arakhin 14b:11:1.hebrew: ליפרקו אגב ארעייהו - ליפדו את האילנות יחד עם הקרקע, שהרי מקום מושב האילן נפדה בחמשים שקל לכור, ואז ולהדרו לבעלים אגב ארעייהו, אם מכרן והגיע היובל. ואמאי אמר מכר אילנות ולא גאלם אין חוזרין לבעלים ביובל:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:11:1.english: Let them be redeemed on account of their land - [Let the trees be redeemed together with] the place where the tree stands, and let them return to the owners on account of their land, if he sold them and the Jubilee arrived. Why, then, did [Rav Pappa] say that if he sold trees and did not [first] redeem them, they do not return to the owners in the Jubilee?:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:12:1.hebrew: משיפולא - מקום מושב האילן עד תהומו:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:12:1.english: From the bottom - The place where the tree sits [i.e., is rooted], down to its depths:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:12:2.hebrew: מחמת טענה - שטוענו הלוקח שהזכיר לו המוכר שם קרקע:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:12:2.english: Due to a claim - [This means] that [the purchaser] claims that [the seller] mentioned the word "land" to him:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:13:1.hebrew: בענין שדה מקנה כתיב (שם כז): וחשב לו הכהן את מכסת הערכך:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:13:1.english: Regarding a purchased field, it is written (Leviticus 27): "Then the priest shall reckon for him the worth of your valuation":

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:13:2.hebrew: לפי שנאמר - בגאולת שדה אחוזה: "זרע חומר שעורים":
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:13:2.english: Since it is stated - with regard to the redemption of an ancestral field: "[An area of] the sowing of a ḥomer of barley seed":

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:13:3.hebrew: ת"ל מכסת - מנין דמיו, דהיינו שויין:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:13:3.english: The verse states "mikhsat" (worth) - [This means] the count of its money, that is, its value:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:14:1.hebrew: נאמר כאן - "וחשב" בשדה מקנה, ולהלן נאמר "וחשב" בשדה אחוזה:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:14:1.english: It is stated here - [the word "shall reckon"] with regard to a purchased field, and there [it is stated "shall reckon"] with regard to an ancestral field:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:14:2.english: A fixed amount - fifty [shekels of] silver:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:15:1.hebrew: מי אית להו הך גזירה שוה - הנלמדת מדוחשב, ומפקי ליה לחומש, למילף חומש אשדה מקנה משדה אחוזה:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:15:1.english: Do they hold of this verbal analogy - [that is derived from] "shall reckon," and they use it to derive the [requirement of the] fifth, [namely] to learn [the law of] the fifth for a purchased field from the field of inheritance:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:16:1.hebrew: חומש בשדה אחוזה ובמקדיש בית - בפרשת בחקתי. וחומש דבהמה טמאה וטהורה, ומעשר שני נמי, התם כתיב:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:16:1.english: The fifth in the case of an ancestral field and of one who consecrates a house - [is written] in the portion of Bechukotai. And the fifth [mentioned] with regard to an animal, whether unclean or clean, and [the fifth of] second tithe as well, is written there [in that same portion]:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:18:1.hebrew: תניא כוותיה דרבא - דאין חומש בשדה מקנה:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:18:1.english: It is taught [in a baraita] in accordance with [the view of] Rava - that there is no [additional] one-fifth [when redeeming] a purchased field:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:18:2.hebrew: ולא מטעמיה - דאילו טעמא דרבא הוא מדגלי קרא חומש בכל הנך דוכתי, וטעמא דברייתא הוא מדהיקישו לערכין, לאדם שהעריך עצמו או חבירו:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:18:2.english: But not for his reason - For Rava's reason is because the verse revealed [the requirement of] an added fifth in all of those places, whereas the reason of the baraita is because [the verse] juxtaposed [a purchased field] to valuations [of a person], [that is,] to a person who valued himself or his fellow:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:19:1.hebrew: המית בן חורין נותן שויו - דכתיב במועד (שמות כ״א:ל׳): אם כופר יושת עליו וגו', ותניא בב"ק (דף מ.): ונתן פדיון נפשו — דמי ניזק:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:19:1.english: [If the ox] killed a freeman, he pays his value - For it is written regarding a forewarned ox (Exodus 21:30): "If a ransom is laid upon him, etc.," and it is taught in a baraita in Bava Kamma (40a): "And he shall give the redemption of his life" — [this means] the value of the one who was harmed:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:19:2.hebrew: חבל בזה ובזה - בין בעבד בין בבן חורין, ולא המיתו, משלם נזק שלם:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:19:2.english: [If it] injured this one and that one - whether a slave or a freeman, and it did not kill him, [the owner] pays full damages:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:20:1.hebrew: במועד אין בתם לא - אסיפא קאי, דקתני: חבל בזה ובזה כו'. דרישא פשיטא לן דקנס דעבד לא שייך בתם, דכתיב: "בתם ובעל השור נקי", ואמרי' בב"ק בפ' שור שנגח ארבעה וחמשה (דף מב.): "נקי" מדמי עבד. וקתני נמי: המית בן חורין, נותן שויו. ודמי כופר לא שייך בתם, דהתם נמי אמרינן: "נקי" מחצי כופר:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:20:1.english: "With a forewarned ox, yes; with an innocuous one, no" - This refers to the latter clause [of the mishna], which teaches: "If it injured this one and that one," etc. For regarding the first clause, it is obvious to us that the fine for a slave does not apply to an innocuous ox, as it is written, "[the ox shall be stoned, and its owner shall be] clear" (Exodus 21:28) — and we say in Bava Kamma, in the chapter [entitled] Shor SheNagach Arba'a VeChamisha (42a): "Clear" [means exempt] from the price of a slave. And it also teaches: [If the ox] killed a freeman, [the owner] pays his value. But the ransom payment does not apply to an innocuous ox, for there too we say: "Clear" [means exempt] from half the ransom:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:20:2.hebrew: אף תם שחבל באדם וכו' - בב"ק בפ' המניח את הכד: תנן שני שוורים תמים שחבלו זה בזה כו', ר' עקיבא אומר: אף תם שחבל באדם משלם במותר נזק שלם. והיינו "במותר": אם חבל גם האדם בשור, ושמו בית דין חבלה שבאדם יותר על חבלה שבשור, בעל השור משלם אותו מותר נזק שלם. אלמא, תם שחבל באדם משלם נזק שלם:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:20:2.english: Even an innocuous ox that injured a person, etc. - In [tractate] Bava Kamma, in the chapter [entitled] "HaMeni'ach et HaKad," [we learned]: Two innocuous oxen that injured each other, etc. Rabbi Akiva says: Even an innocuous ox that injured a person pays full damages for the excess. And this is the meaning of "for the excess": If the person also injured the ox, and the court assessed the injury done to the person as greater than the injury done to the ox, the owner of the ox pays that excess as full damages. Evidently, an innocuous ox that injured a person pays full damages:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:21:1.hebrew: איידי דבעי למיתני סיפא המית עבד המית בן חורין כו' משום הכי - נקט ברישא מועד. והאי דקאמר "סיפא", לאו סיפא ממש, אלא סיפא דרישא היא, דמועד ברישא קתני לה:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:21:1.english: Since [the Tanna] wants to teach in the latter clause, "[an ox that] killed a slave, [an ox that] killed a freeman," etc. — for this reason - he stated "forewarned" in the first clause. And as for what [the Gemara] says, "the latter clause," it does not mean the actual latter clause, but the latter part of the first clause, for he teaches it [the case of the forewarned ox] in the first clause:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:22:1.hebrew: פגם - מפרש בכתובות (ד' מ.): שמין אותה כמה אדם רוצה ליתן בין שפחה בתולה לשפחה בעולה, להשיאה לעבדו, שיש לו קורת רוח הימנו:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:22:1.english: Degradation - [The Gemara] explains in [tractate] Ketubot (40a): We assess her [value] — how much a person would be willing to pay [for the difference] between a virgin maidservant and a non-virgin maidservant, in order to marry her off to his [Canaanite] slave, from whom he derives satisfaction [and whom he therefore wishes to reward]:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:23:1.hebrew: מכל מילי - חמשים סלעים אמר רחמנא ובושת ופגם לא ליתיב ליה:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:23:1.english: For all matters - [the Merciful One stated fifty sela for all matters, and so] he should not have to pay [her] for humiliation and degradation:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:24:1.hebrew: בעל בת הדיוטות כו' - קאמר בתמיה. אבל השתא, כי יהיב בושת, יש חילוק בין בת מלכים לבת הדיוטות:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:24:1.english: One who had intercourse with the daughter of ordinary people, etc. - [He said this] as a rhetorical question. But now, when he pays [for] the humiliation, there is a difference between the daughter of kings and the daughter of ordinary people:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:3:1.hebrew: בתר פדיון - וכיון דבשעת פדיון מת אביו, הויא לה שדה אחוזה:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:3:1.english: After the redemption - And since at the time of the redemption his father had died, it is [considered] an ancestral field:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:5:1.hebrew: א"כ - דלכדר' מאיר הוא דאתא קרא, לכתוב רחמנא וכו':
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:5:1.english: If so - that [the verse] comes [to teach] according to Rabbi Meir, [then] the Merciful One should have written, etc.:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:6:1.english: He redeems them by their value - even though they are ancestral fields:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:7:1.hebrew: לא גאלם - הבעלים ומכרם גזבר לאחר:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:7:1.english: If he did not redeem them - [the owner], and the treasurer sold them to another:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:7:2.hebrew: יוצאין לכהנים ביובל - כדכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:כ״א) ואם לא יגאל וגו', וכתיב: והיה השדה בצאתו ביובל וגו':
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:7:2.english: They go out to the priests in the Jubilee - As it is written (Leviticus 27:21): "And if he will not redeem [the field]..." etc., and it is written: "But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee..." etc.:

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:7:3.hebrew: שדה אמר רחמנא - "והיה השדה בצאתו ביובל" וגו' (שם):
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:7:3.english: "Field," the Merciful One said - "And the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee," etc. (there):

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:8:1.hebrew: פחות משתי שנים - ואע"ג דמוכר קרקע לחבירו אין רשאי לגאול עד שתהא שתי שנים ביד הלוקח, כדכתיב (שם כה): במספר שני תבואות וגו':
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:8:1.english: In less than two years - Even though one who sells land to his fellow may not redeem it until it has been in the hands of the buyer for two years, as it is written (Leviticus 25): "According to the number of years of the crops [he shall sell it to you]":

Rashi on Arakhin 14b:9:1.hebrew: לא גאלם אין יוצאין לכהנים ביובל - אם מכרם גזבר לאחר:
Rashi on Arakhin 14b:9:1.english: [If] he did not redeem them, they do not go out to the priests in the Jubilee - [This applies] if the treasurer sold them to another:

Tosafot on Arakhin 14b:15:1.hebrew: איבעיא להו לרבנן אית להו גז"ש ומפקין ליה לחומש או דלמא כו' - קשה לרבינו אלחנן: אמאי לא נילף מינהון ג"ש? נהי דבנין אב לא ילפינן מינייהו, מ"מ ג"ש נילף מינייהו! ונראה לר', מדאיצטריך למיכתב חומש גבי מקדיש שדה אחוזה וגבי מקדיש את ביתו, ומצינו למילף חד מחבריה בג"ש, ולא ילפינן אלא כתב חומש לכל חד וחד, ש"מ שני כתובין הבאים כאחד ולא ילפינן מינייהו בעלמא, אפילו בג"ש:
Tosafot on Arakhin 14b:15:1.english: A dilemma was raised before them: Do the Rabbis accept the verbal analogy and use it to derive the one-fifth, or perhaps, etc. - Rabbeinu Elchanan found this difficult: Why do we not derive a verbal analogy from them [i.e., from these two cases]? Granted that we do not derive a binyan av (a general principle) from them, nevertheless let us derive a verbal analogy from them! And it seems to Rabbi [Tam] that since it was necessary to write the one-fifth with regard to one who consecrates an inherited field and with regard to one who consecrates his house, and we could have derived one from the other by a verbal analogy, yet we do not derive [it] but rather [the Torah] wrote the one-fifth for each one separately — learn from this that [these are] two verses that come as one, and we do not derive anything else from them, even by a verbal analogy:

Tosafot on Arakhin 14b:16:1.hebrew: (לעיל) הוו להו שני כתובין הבאין כאחד - וא"ת: מה ענין זה לשני כתובין הבאין כאחד? כיון דגבי שדה מקנה איכא ג"ש למילף חומש משדה אחוזה, וגבי מקדיש בית ליכא ג"ש! ושמא הכא דכתיב "והעריך" גבי מקדיש בית, כמאן דכתיב "וחשב". או שמא י"ל: "וחשב" אין זו ג"ש גמורה, אע"ג דקרי ליה הספר ג"ש. וה"נ אשכחן בפ"ק דב"ק (דף ו:) גבי "נאמר שדה למעלה ונאמר שדה למטה", קרי ליה התם ג"ש, ואור"י דאינו ג"ש גמורה. או שמא י"ל משום דכתיב קודש גבי מקדיש שדה אחוזה, וכתיב נמי קודש [גבי] מקדיש בית, וקודש קודש ג"ש גמורה היא, מש"ה קרי ליה ב' כתובין הבאים כאחד:
Tosafot on Arakhin 14b:16:1.english: (Earlier:) They are two verses that come as one - And if you ask: What does this have to do with two verses that come as one? Since in the case of a purchased field there is a verbal analogy to learn the added fifth from an ancestral field, whereas in the case of one who consecrates a house there is no verbal analogy! Perhaps here, where "and he shall assess" is written regarding one who consecrates a house, it is as if "and he shall calculate" were written. Or perhaps one can say: "and he shall calculate" is not a complete verbal analogy, even though the Gemara calls it a verbal analogy. And so too we find in the first chapter of Bava Kamma (6b), regarding "it was stated 'field' above and it was stated 'field' below," that [the Gemara] there calls it a verbal analogy, and Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that it is not a complete verbal analogy. Or perhaps one can say that [the Gemara calls it this] because "holy" is written regarding one who consecrates an ancestral field, and "holy" is also written [regarding] one who consecrates a house, and "holy, holy" is a complete verbal analogy; therefore it calls them two verses that come as one:

Tosafot on Arakhin 14b:20:1.hebrew: במועד אין בתם לא לימא מתני' דלא כרבי עקיבא כו' - אסיפא דסיפא קאי, דקתני "חבל בזה ובזה משלם נזק שלם". אבל לא מצי למימר דקאי אהמית העבד ולא אהמית בן חורין, דבהא לא פליג רבי עקיבא, דתם אינו משלם לא כופר ולא שלשים של עבד, כדאיתא בב"ק בפ' שור שנגח ד' וה' (בבא קמא דף מב:):
Tosafot on Arakhin 14b:20:1.english: "With a forewarned ox, yes; with an innocuous one, no. Let us say that the mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Akiva," etc. - [The Gemara's question] refers to the last clause of the latter part [of the mishna], which teaches: "If it injured [a person] in this case and in that case, he pays full damages." But one cannot say that it refers to [the case where the ox] killed the slave and not [the case where it killed] a freeman, for in this Rabbi Akiva does not disagree, [namely] that [the owner of] an innocuous ox pays neither ransom nor the thirty [shekels] of a slave, as is stated in Bava Kamma, in the chapter [entitled] Shor SheNagach Arba'a VeHamesh (Bava Kamma 42b):

Tosafot on Arakhin 14b:22:1.hebrew: בושת הכל לפי המבייש והמתבייש - ופגם מפרש בכתובות (דף מ:): אומדים כמה אדם רוצה ליתן בשפחה בתולה יותר מבעולה, להשיאה לעבדו שעשה לו קורת רוח:
Tosafot on Arakhin 14b:22:1.english: [The payment for] humiliation is all according to the one who humiliates and the one who is humiliated - And [the payment for] degradation is explained in [tractate] Ketubot (40b): They assess how much a person would be willing to pay for a virgin maidservant [rather than] a non-virgin, in order to marry her to his [Canaanite] slave, [an arrangement] that gave him [the master] satisfaction:

Tosafot on Arakhin 14b:24:1.hebrew: יאמרו בת מלכים חמשים בת הדיוט חמשים - יש תימה קצת: דבמשנה תני "אחד הגדולה שבכהונה ואחד הקטנה שבישראל נותן חמשים", ומאי שנא דהכא מזכיר בגמ' הגדולה "בת מלכים", ובמשנה תנא "גדולה שבכהונה"?:
Tosafot on Arakhin 14b:24:1.english: They will say: a daughter of kings, fifty; a daughter of an ordinary person, fifty - There is some difficulty: for in the Mishnah it is taught, "Both the greatest [woman] among the priesthood and the lowliest among Israel — he pays fifty [sela]." And what is different that here the Gemara mentions the greatest [as] "a daughter of kings," while in the Mishnah it taught "the greatest among the priesthood"?:
